title: docker/e2e/selftest.sh: an assertion appended after its own reporting line runs, can fail, and the exit code stays 0
description:
Confirmed empirically 2026-09-17, prompted by a cross-repo pattern report (opum-cli-e2e's
test/selftest.mjs, TASK-61: an assertion appended after a hand-rolled harness's own reporting block
runs, can fail, and is never counted). Checked lore-cli's own hand-rolled assertion scripts for the
same shape rather than taking the report on faith.

THREE OTHER SCRIPTS SCANNED, NEITHER AFFECTED: docker/e2e/lib/steps.sh (the shared helper library --
owns the PASS/FAIL counters but has no summary/exit block of its own, so the defect can't live here).
scripts/assert-main-fast-forward.sh (two assertions, one unconditional final block whose last line is
a bare echo, not an early conditional exit -- not vulnerable). scripts/readme-readback.sh (a
state-machine confirmation script with structured per-branch exits, not an accumulating-counter
harness -- not the same shape at all).

docker/e2e/selftest.sh IS AFFECTED, confirmed by the exact method opum-cli-e2e used: append a
deliberately-failing assertion after its own reporting line and run it.

REPRODUCTION (no container needed -- that is the whole point of this script):
  mkdir -p /tmp/probe/lib
  cp docker/e2e/lib/steps.sh /tmp/probe/lib/steps.sh
  cp docker/e2e/selftest.sh /tmp/probe/selftest.sh
  cat >> /tmp/probe/selftest.sh <<'EOF'
  expect pass "deliberately wrong expectation" -- false
  EOF
  bash /tmp/probe/selftest.sh; echo "exit: $?"

RESULT: the printed summary line ("==== harness selftest: 28 ok, 0 bad ====") is IDENTICAL to an
unmodified run -- the appended probe is not counted into it at all. The probe's own failure IS
printed below that summary line ("[BAD]  deliberately wrong expectation -- expected the helper to say
pass, it said fail"), so a human reading the whole log top to bottom can still see it, but it is not
counted -- and the part that matters for CI: THE SCRIPT'S EXIT CODE IS 0. A confirmed, named, failing
assertion produces exit 0.

ROOT CAUSE, located: selftest.sh's own tail (current lines 149-150) is

  printf '\n==== harness selftest: %s ok, %s bad ====\n' "$SELF_PASS" "$SELF_FAIL"
  [ "$SELF_FAIL" -eq 0 ] || exit 1

This is a CONDITIONAL exit: it only calls exit when SELF_FAIL is nonzero AT THAT LINE. If SELF_FAIL
is 0 at that point (true for every case that exists today), the test evaluates true, no exit is
called, and execution falls off the end of the script -- or, if anything follows, continues into it.
Bash's exit code then becomes whatever the LAST command executed returns, unrelated to SELF_FAIL's
value by the time the process actually terminates. Nothing re-checks SELF_FAIL after this line.

CONTRAST WITH docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh, which shares the same two-part shape (tally-then-exit) but is
NOT vulnerable to this specific defect -- worth recording so nobody assumes fixing selftest.sh covers
both. run-e2e.sh's tail (lines 2025-2053) prints tally() and THEN, unconditionally, re-evaluates the
LIVE $FAIL/$REPORT_WRITE_FAILURES globals in an if/exit block whose own last line is a bare `exit 0`.
Code appended between the tally print and that block still correctly flips the exit code (only the
PRINTED tally text would read stale -- a visibility gap, not a correctness one); code appended AFTER
the literal `exit 0` is simply unreachable dead code, not silent miscounting. Different and lesser
risk. Not this defect.

WHY THIS MATTERS, not just in principle: `bash docker/e2e/selftest.sh` is a required CI step
(.github/workflows/ci.yml:621-622, "Prove the E2E assertion helpers discriminate"), and its own
comment says why it runs first -- "a broken assertion helper invalidates every case in the harness
below". Its entire reason to exist, per its own header comment quoting LCLI-360, is that a helper's
discrimination must be OBSERVED, not assumed. The one property it does not currently prove about
itself is that IT stays a gate as it grows -- exactly what LCLI-360 demanded of the helpers it tests.

FIX SHAPE, not prescribed: remove the conditional-exit idiom rather than patch around it, e.g.
compute the final exit code unconditionally right before returning it (the same
recheck-live-globals-immediately-before-exit pattern run-e2e.sh already uses at its own tail), so the
property holds no matter where in the file a future case gets added -- not just past the current last
line.

acceptanceCriteria.text: selftest.sh correctly exits nonzero when a case appended after its current reporting line fails -- proven the same way this task found the defect: append a deliberately-failing case at the true end of the file and confirm the exit code flips to nonzero.

The fix removes the conditional-exit idiom at the tail rather than adding a second check after it, so the property holds regardless of where in the file a future case is added, not only past the line that is currently last.
run-e2e.sh is left alone unless review finds it shares this defect (this task confirmed it does not, see description); if it is changed anyway, the change and the reasoning are recorded here.

The regression test is mutation-tested: revert the fix and confirm the same deliberately-failing appended case regresses to exit 0, so the test is proven sensitive to the defect rather than merely present.

finalSummary: Fixed and delivered in PR #178. DEFECT REPRODUCED before fixing, by the exact method the task prescribed: append a deliberately-failing case after selftest.sh's reporting line and run it. The printed summary read '28 ok, 0 bad' -- byte-identical to an unmodified run -- the appended probe's own [BAD] line printed BELOW that summary, and THE SCRIPT EXITED 0. A confirmed, named, failing assertion produced exit 0 in a REQUIRED CI step whose entire reason to exist is that a gate must be observed failing rather than assumed to work. ROOT CAUSE: the tail was a CONDITIONAL exit, [ $SELF_FAIL -eq 0 ] || exit 1, which calls exit only when SELF_FAIL is already nonzero AT THAT LINE. With SELF_FAIL at 0 -- true for every case that exists today -- no exit is called, execution falls off the end, and bash's status becomes whatever ran last. AC#2 SATISFIED BY REMOVING THE IDIOM, not by adding a second check after it: the verdict moved into the EXIT handler. The reasoning, and it is measured rather than argued -- a trailing check only ever sees cases inserted ABOVE itself, and appending at the END of the file is exactly how this arrives, so a trailing guard is structurally blind to the next occurrence of the bug it was added for. opum-cli-e2e measured this directly on their own harness (TASK-61): their first version WAS a plain if at the bottom and a deliberately appended section walked straight past it. The handler also absorbs the pre-existing cleanup trap, because bash permits only ONE EXIT trap and registering a second would have silently replaced the cleanup and leaked the temp directory -- a defect the fix would have introduced had it not been noticed. Counters read ${...:-0} since the handler registers before they initialize, and exit $rc preserves a non-verdict failure rather than flattening it. BONUS, beyond the minimum: the summary is now CORRECT and not merely fatal -- the appended case is COUNTED ('28 ok, 1 bad') where it previously read '0 bad', which is how this survived being looked at. AC#1 PROVED both directions as separate measurements: clean tree green at exit 0; appended failure red at exit 1. AC#4 MUTATION: reverting the fix regresses the appended case to exit 0 and reddens exactly the new regression test, while that test's clean-run assertion stays green -- so the test is sensitive to the defect rather than always red. AC#3: run-e2e.sh untouched -- git diff origin/dev -- docker/e2e/run-e2e.sh is EMPTY. It shares the tally-then-exit shape but re-evaluates the live globals unconditionally before its own bare exit 0, so it is not vulnerable to this; no change was made and none was needed. EVIDENCE: CI run 35407345434 on head d8d78e34 -- all five contexts required by dev's ruleset concluded PASS with zero non-pass jobs anywhere. shellcheck clean over 7 tracked scripts; full suite 3287 pass / 0 fail; typecheck and lint exit 0.
